courses.subject: CSAT
courses.title: Media and Representation: History and Theory

schedule.class_attributes: Can, change to Eng if needed

courses.description: This course reviews the history and theory of media in artistic and spatial representation. It covers the development of various media forms from the late 20th century to the present, including paper-based, screen-based, 3D, and immersive spatial representation. Students will gain knowledge of how representation formats evolve in accordance with new technology and social conditions. They will be engaged in discussions on how they affect our perception and creation of the urban environment.
courses.academic_group: Sch of Arch & Sch of JL & Comm
courses.academic_org: Sch of Arch & Sch of JL & Comm
courses.learning_outcomes:
After completing this course, students will be able to:
1. Describe major concepts in and development in media and representation and explain how they relate to changing social, cultural, and technological conditions.
2. Analyse how different representational forms shape perception, experience, and the communication of ideas in artistic and spatial contexts.
3. Compare historical and contemporary approaches to artistic and spatial representation using appropriate critical concepts and vocabulary.
4. Apply media and representation theory to case studies in art, design, architecture, communication, or digital culture.
5. Reflect on the ethical, cultural, and environmental implications of representation technologies in contemporary practice.

courses.subject: CSAT
courses.title: Creative Dialogue
courses.description: This course facilitates participatory dialogues with practitioners on arts, design, and technology. Through case studies, discussions, reflection and exchange, students will gain an understanding of how creative disciplines intersect with social and cultural contexts. The dialogues will focus on technology-enabled creative works across the fields of arts, media, theatre, and architecture, beyond their disciplinary boundaries. Students are expected to take an active role in designing and curating the conservation, and to reflect upon how it shapes contemporary life and environment.
courses.academic_group: Sch of Arch & Sch of JL & Comm
courses.academic_org: Sch of Arch & Sch of JL & Comm
courses.learning_outcomes:
After completing this course, students will be able to:
1. Comprehend key ideas and practices in arts, design, media, architecture, and related creative fields.
2. Critically examine creative work in relation to its social, cultural, historical, and technological context.
3. Engage thoughtfully in dialogue with practitioners and peers to draw informed observations and reflective insights.
4. Interpreted interdisciplinary creative ideas, processes, and narratives with openness and critical awareness, to reflect upon their own assumptions/positions and to situate them within a broader cultural landscape.
5. Synthesise course learning into reflective, analytical, and creative responses.
